basis: Disorder of eosinophils, a blood-cell lineage; the umbrella does not establish immunodeficiency or common tissue injury.
Inherited calcium-regulation disorder; paresthesias and muscle spasms are symptoms, while basal ganglia calcification occurs in only 5-29%.
Defining biliary, neurologic and skeletal abnormalities; developmental delay 4/6 and polydactyly 4/7; renal insufficiency 2/6 (~33%) supports renal involvement.
Malignant epithelial tumour arising in the colon or rectum.
Adrenal aldosterone excess with hypertension as a defining manifestation; hypokalemia is endocrine/metabolic, and cerebral hemorrhage is occasional.
Inherited complement immunodeficiency; recurrent Neisserial infections are susceptibility-related diseases, not established chronic neurologic damage.
Familial restrictive cardiomyopathy; hepatomegaly and ascites in 1/2 do not alone establish hepatic tissue injury or loss of function.
Carcinoma originating in renal collecting-duct epithelium.
Tick-borne Borrelia infection; no additional organ has established direct damage in at least 30% of typical cases.
Congenital clasped-thumb deformity affects the locomotor apparatus; the nonspecific, unquantified nervous-system annotation does not establish common neurologic damage.
Exocrine pancreatic carcinoma; osteoclast-like cells within the tumour do not indicate bone involvement.
Pathologic overgrowth of gingival tissue; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Mesenchymal connective-tissue hamartoma, with no specified organ site; liver and subcutaneous locations are subtype-specific.
Localized skin disorder characterized by hypopigmentation and fine scaling.
Defining developmental brain disease and myopathy; strabismus reported in 1/1 assessed patient supports ocular dysfunction, with frequency uncertain in this very small series.
Benign immature adipose-tissue tumour, typically occupying subcutaneous tissue; deep locations do not establish common muscle involvement.
Early-onset lens cataract; broader ancestral CRYAB-associated muscle and cardiac disorders are not established features of this specific concept.
COL9A1-related epiphyseal and joint dysplasia, with osteoarthritis and vertebral abnormalities; no additional organ involvement established.
Congenital deficiency of hair growth; ocular disease occurs in particular syndromic subtypes rather than across the umbrella.
Pancreatic epithelial adenoma classified under digestive-system neoplasms; no endocrine-cell origin or hormone syndrome is specified.
Neurocutaneous NF1 deletion; joint hypermobility 21/29 and progressive visual loss 30-79%; cardiac abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap; Lisch nodules non-damaging.
Histidine metabolism disorder defined here by encephalopathy, intellectual disability and ataxia; nystagmus is neurologic, and recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Inherited temporal-lobe epilepsy with focal seizures and childhood febrile seizures.
Immune-mediated fibrosing thyroid disease; vocal-cord paralysis and tracheal stenosis occur in 5-29%; extracervical fibrosing diseases are rare or separately diagnosed.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and epiphyses, with osteoporosis, joint deformity and osteoarthritis; no additional organ damage established.
